questions.question: Which form of farming is called ‘slash and burn’ agriculture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Primitive subsistence farming.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slash-and-burn agriculture** is a type of farming in which forests are burned and cleared to make way for crops.
 
• Slash and burn agriculture is **primitive subsistence farming.**__
 
• The ‘slash and burn agriculture is known as **‘Milpa’** in Mexico and Central America.
 
• **Shifting cultivation** is also known as ‘slash and burn agriculture.
 
• The initial step in the technique is to clear an area of trees and woody plants.
 __
 
• The "slash," or felled vegetation, is then allowed to dry, usually just before the rainy season starts.
 
• The biomass is then burned, producing a nutrient-rich layer of ash that fertilises the soil while temporarily eliminating weed and pest species.
 
• Due to nutrient depletion and weed and pest invasion, the plot's output diminishes after three to five years, compelling the farmers to quit the field and shift to a new place.
 
• Due to a shortage of natural fertilisers and insecticides, among other things, productivity is low.
 
 
 
• Slash and burn agriculture will lead to **deforestation.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8efaef53ff23a2b542c6377416fdb16f3da34c0c88e26fbd23d03f192d3905e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intensive subsistence agriculture** is a type of farming in which farmers cultivates a small plot of land using simple tools and more labour.
 
• **Commercial farming** is a kind of farming that employs bigger doses of contemporary inputs in order to increase output.
 
• **Hydroponic farming**, often known as soilless farming, is a method of growing plants without the use of soil.

questions.question: In which of the soil conservation methods in the coastal and dry regions, rows of trees are planted to check the wind movement to protect soil cover?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shelter belts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shelter belts are rows of** trees and shrubs planted to protect soil from wind erosion, particularly in coastal and arid regions.**
 
• These tree lines reduce wind **speed across the ground and thereby decrease the wind's ability to lift and carry soil particles away, combating wind erosion effectively.**
 
• Apart from reducing **wind erosion, shelter belts also offer additional benefits like providing habitat for wildlife, sequestering carbon, and enhancing the landscape's aesthetics.**
 
• This method is quite common in **flat, dry regions where wind erosion is a major issue, such as parts of North America, Africa, and Asia.**
 
• Shelter belts can take the form of **single or multiple rows of trees or shrubs,** depending on the severity of the wind erosion problem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulching:**

 
 
• Mulching involves covering the soil surface with a layer of organic or inorganic material **(like straw, leaves, compost, or plastic sheets).**
 
• This technique **retains soil moisture, suppresses weed growth, and can also prevent soil erosion by reducing the impact of raindrops on the soil surface.**
 
 
 
• **Rock Dam:**
 
 
• Rock dams are barriers built across channels, gullies, or small waterways using rocks.
 
• They slow down the flow of water, reduce its erosive power and trap sediments.
 
• **This technique is commonly used in mountainous regions or areas prone to flash floods and gully erosion.**
 
 
 
• **Contour Barriers:**
 
 
• **​**Contour barriers are physical barriers like **stones, vegetation, or soil bunds constructed along the contours of a slope.**
 
• **They slow down water runoff, promote water infiltration, and reduce soil erosion by water.**
 
• This method is typically used on sloping land in both farming and forestry.

questions.question: How many agro-climatic zones (ACZ) are characterized by the Planning Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15.**__

__
 
• 15 agro-climatic zones (ACZ) are characterized by the Planning Commission of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• An Agro-climatic zone is a** land unit in form of major climates **that are suitable for a certain range of crops and cultivators. 
 
• **National Agricultural Research Project (NARP) was launched by ICAR** for initiating agricultural research in the agro-climatic zones of the country.
 
 
• The purpose was to set up and upgrade a zonal research station in each agro-climatic zone for creating location-specific, need-based research targeted for specific agro-ecological situations.
 
• In NARP, the country is divided into **127 agro-climatic zones.**
 
 
 
• The agro-climatic zone division helps to achieve optimum utilization in a suitable manner within the framework of resource constraints and potentials of each region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Planning Commission of India:
 
 
• The Planning Commission formulated India's Five-Year Plans.
 
• It was formed in** March 1950.**
 
• It was **replaced by NITI Aayog **in the year **2015.**
 
 
 
• NITI Aayog:
 
 
• ​NITI Aayog or National Institution for Transforming India Aayog is the replacement of Planning Commission of India.

questions.question: Use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation is referred to as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**intensive cultivation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation is referred to as** ****intensive cultivation**.
 
• **Intensive agriculture, **also referred to as intensive farming, conventional agriculture, or industrial agriculture, is characterized by the significant utilization of labor and capital in relation to land area.
 
• It involves higher levels of input and output per unit of agricultural land area compared to extensive farming practices.
 
• In contrast, extensive farming involves cultivating large farms with relatively smaller inputs, such as cash and labor, and is typically practiced in regions with extensive land and sparse population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Extensive farming,** also known as extensive agriculture, is characterized by the use of minimal inputs of labor, fertilizers, and capital in relation to the land area being farmed. 
 
• **Hybrid cultivation **involves the cross-breeding of two different varieties of plants to combine desired traits. 
 
• **In a Capitalistic farming system,** farming activities are directed and managed by individual entrepreneurs who exercise control over the agricultural processes.

questions.question: What is meant by subsistence agriculture?

options.text: Agricultural output is sufficient for the country.
Agriculturists produce primarily for the market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculturists produce primarily for themselves.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Subsistence agriculture:-
 
 
• **It refers to a type of farming where farmers produce primarily for themselves and their families, rather than for the market.**
 
• Farmers who practice subsistence agriculture typically have small plots of land and use traditional farming methods.
 
• The crops they grow are usually basic staples like rice, corn, or beans, which they consume themselves or trade with other farmers for other goods.
 
• Subsistence agriculture is often associated with rural or developing areas where people may not have access to modern technology or infrastructure.
 
• While subsistence agriculture can provide a reliable food source for farmers and their families, it may not generate enough income to support a higher standard of living or promote economic growth.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the consequences of the Green Revolution?

options.text: Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment In cash to payment in kind (grain)
The rich grew richer and many of the poor stagnated or grew poorer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment In cash to payment in kind (grain) **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** states that "Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain)" is a consequence of the Green Revolution, which is not correct.
 
• The Green Revolution primarily focused on increasing agricultural productivity through the use of high-yield variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.
 
• **Wages of agricultural workers increased** (Option 2) and **Employment of agricultural workers increased** (Option 3) are true outcomes of the Green Revolution.
 
• Option 4, **The rich grew richer and many of the poor stagnated or grew poorer**, is also a recognized consequence of the Green Revolution, as it often benefited wealthier farmers more than the poorer ones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution was introduced in the 1960s and 1970s to combat food shortages in developing countries like India.
 
• It led to a significant increase in food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, through the adoption of new agricultural techniques and technologies.
 
• While it improved food security and reduced famine, it also resulted in socioeconomic disparities and environmental issues such as soil degradation and increased use of chemical fertilizers.

questions.question: The Green Revolution led to an increase in the agricultural output primarily due to the use of HYV seeds. Here, HYV refers to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Yielding Variety**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **High Yielding Variety (HYV)** refers to seeds that are engineered to produce more crops per area planted compared to traditional varieties.
 
• The introduction of **HYV seeds** was a crucial component of the Green Revolution, which significantly boosted agricultural productivity, particularly in developing countries.
 
• These seeds are often more resistant to pests and diseases and can grow in a variety of climatic conditions, making them highly adaptable.
 
• The use of **HYV seeds** typically requires the application of modern agricultural techniques, including the use of fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• While HYV seeds have contributed to increased food production, they also necessitate careful management to avoid issues such as soil degradation and water resource depletion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** began in the 1960s and was marked by the adoption of new agricultural technologies, including HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• It led to a substantial increase in food grain production, particularly in countries like India and Mexico.
 
• The Green Revolution played a significant role in transforming agriculture from subsistence farming to commercial farming, making many countries self-sufficient in food production.
 
• However, the Green Revolution also brought challenges such as environmental damage, increased inequality among farmers, and the marginalization of smallholders.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the impacts of the green revolution?

options.text: A loosening of traditional bonds or hereditary relationships between farmers or landowners and agricultural workers.
The rise of a class of 'free' wage labourers.
A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain).
There was an increase in the use of agricultural labour as cultivation became more intensive.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain)**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A shift from payment in cash** to payment in kind (grain) is NOT one of the impacts of the **green revolution**.
 
• **Payment-in-kind (PIK)** involves utilizing a commodity or service as compensation rather than cash.
 
• Additionally, it pertains to a financial instrument that provides interest or dividends to bondholders, note holders, or preferred stockholders through the issuance of additional securities or equity instead of cash.
 
• PIK securities are appealing to companies that wish to avoid cash expenditures and are frequently employed in leveraged buyouts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Green Revolution** denotes a historical period spanning from the 1940s to the 1960s, characterized by the development of high-yielding varieties of crops, notably wheat and rice, aimed at boosting food production.
 
• Its primary objective was to mitigate poverty and malnutrition by enhancing crop yields.
 
• The Green Revolution embraced innovative farming techniques and the introduction of new crop varieties, including: 
 
 
• High-yielding variety seeds
 
• Mechanized farm tools
 
• Irrigation facilities
 
• Pesticides
 
• Fertilizers
 
 
 
• Norman Borlaug is acclaimed as the **"Father of the Green Revolution."**
 
• In 1970, he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his efforts in pioneering the development of High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat.

questions.question: Which of the following recommends Minimum Support Prices for crops in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices**__

 __
 
• It was formed in **January 1965**.
 
• It recommends the **minimum support prices (MSP)** and **issues prices for paddy and wheat.**
 
• It is a joint office of the ministry of agriculture & farmers welfare.
 
• It raises productivity and overall grain production in line with the emerging demand patterns in the country.
 
• It recommends MSPs of** 23 commodities**, are following:
 
 
• **7 oilseeds** including groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sesamum, sunflower, safflower, and nigerseed.
 
• **7 kinds of cereal** including paddy, wheat, maize, sorghum, pearl millet, barley, and ragi.
 
• **5 pulses** including gram, tur, moong, urad, and lentil.
 
• **4 commercial crops** include copra, sugarcane, cotton, and raw jute.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research**__

 __
 
• ICAR was **first reorganized in 1965.**
 
• The **Indian Council of Agricultural Research is an autonomous organization.**
 
• It is under the **Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.**
 
• **Headquarters**- New Delhi.
 
• There is a total of **101 ICAR institutes and 71 agricultural universities **spread across the country.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**__
 
 
• **NITI Aayog **is **not a** constitutional body. 
 
• It was **established on January 1, 2015.**
 
• It is formed in place of the Planning Commission. o The** ex-officio Chairman of this is the Prime Minister.**
 
• It is the premier policy **Think Tank of the Government of India**, providing both directional and policy inputs.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT true of the second phase of the green revolution?

options.text: It was launched in areas with a significant shift from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation.
It covered the period of the 1980s.
It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
It was adopted by farmers living in dry and semi-arid regions of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The second phase of the Green Revolution, which occurred in the 1980s,
 
 
• aimed to expand the benefits of the Green Revolution to areas with less favourable conditions, such as dry and semi-arid regions.
 
 
 
• **First Phase (1960s-1970s):**
 
 
• Focused on introducing high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds and chemical fertilizers to increase agricultural production.
 
• Primarily targeted areas with adequate irrigation facilities, such as the Punjab and Haryana regions.
 
 
 
• **Second Phase (1980s):**
 
 
• Expanded the Green Revolution to areas with less favorable conditions, including dry and semi-arid regions.
 
• Introduced drought-resistant and early-maturing crop varieties.
 
• Promoted integrated pest management and soil conservation practices.
 
• Emphasized the need for sustainable agriculture to reduce environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Therefore, the statement "It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s" is incorrect.**
 
 
• The second phase of the Green Revolution took place in the 1980s, building upon the successes of the first phase and aiming to further enhance agricultural productivity and food security in India.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Green Revolution is/are correct?

I. India became self-reliant after the advent of the Green Revolution.

II. Due to the Green Revolution, the soil started losing nutrients due to repeated cultivation of the same crop.

III. Green revolution caused depletion of fresh ground water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i, ii and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India led to self-reliance in terms of food grain production, transforming the country from a food-deficient nation to one that could sustain itself.
 
• Repetitive cultivation of the same high-yield variety (HYV) crops led to soil nutrient depletion, as these crops absorbed specific nutrients in large quantities.
 
• The Green Revolution intensified the use of water resources for irrigation, leading to the depletion of fresh groundwater levels, especially in regions like Punjab and Haryana.
 
• The use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides increased significantly during the Green Revolution, contributing to environmental degradation and impacting soil health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period during the 1960s and 1970s when agriculture in many developing countries was transformed by the adoption of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• It aimed to increase food production to combat hunger and improve food security.
 
• Countries like India and Mexico saw significant increases in crop production, particularly in wheat and rice.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental issues, including soil degradation, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Soil Nutrient Depletion:**
 
 
• Continuous cultivation of the same crop without crop rotation can lead to the depletion of specific nutrients in the soil.
 
• This results in reduced soil fertility, necessitating the increased use of chemical fertilizers to maintain crop yields.
 
• Over time, this can lead to soil degradation and reduced agricultural sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater Depletion:**
 
 
• Intensive irrigation practices, particularly in regions with limited water resources, can lead to the over-extraction of groundwater.
 
• This can cause a decline in water tables, making it more difficult and expensive to access water for irrigation in the long term.
 
• Regions like Punjab and Haryana in India have experienced significant groundwater depletion due to the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides associated with the Green Revolution has led to environmental pollution.
 
• These chemicals can contaminate soil and water bodies, adversely affecting plant and animal life.
 
• There are also health concerns for humans exposed to these chemicals through food and water.

questions.question: The Green Revolution was due to the introduction of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high yielding varieties of seeds**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution** was primarily due to the introduction of **high yielding varieties of seeds**.
 
• This revolution started in the 1960s in India and significantly increased agricultural production, especially in wheat and rice.
 
• Other factors contributing to the Green Revolution included the use of fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation techniques, but the high yielding varieties of seeds were the cornerstone.
 
• The main aim was to make India self-sufficient in food grains and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• The Green Revolution had a significant impact on food security and rural development in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution was led by agricultural scientists like **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan** in India.
 
• It was part of a larger initiative supported by international organizations such as the **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** and the **International Rice Research Institute (IRRI)**.
 
• The high yielding varieties of seeds were developed through cross-breeding and genetic modifications to increase resistance to pests and diseases.
 
• Although the Green Revolution had many benefits, it also led to environmental issues such as soil degradation, overuse of water resources, and increased use of chemical inputs.

questions.question: Which type of seeds played an important role in Green Revolution in India?
questions.solution:

• The movement lasted from 1967 to 1978 and was a great success.
 
 
 
• This was coupled with better and efficient irrigation and the correct use of fertilizers to boost the crop.
 
 
• The result of the Green Revolution was to make India self-sufficient when it came to food grains.
 
 
 
• These HYV seeds had more success with the wheat crop and were highly effective in regions that had proper irrigation.

questions.question: What type of trees are found in the northern central Himalayan range (1801 to 3001 m) and the southern Nilgiri high mountain ranges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Oak, Junipers, or Maple.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Montane Temperate Forest, **These types of forests are mainly generated in the Northern middle Himalayas ranges (1801 to 3001 Meters) and Southern Nilgiri higher Mountain ranges.
 
• Some significant trees of a montane temperate forest are **rhododendrons, ferns, oak, maple, juniper, deodar, chilgoza**, etc.
 
• These types of forests are found in the state of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are mainly two types of tropical forests that are found in the Himalayas - the **tropical rainforests, and the tropical deciduous forests**.
 
• The tropical rainforests are dense, evergreen, gloomy, and, similar to the forests of the Amazon basin and other equatorial areas.
 
• **Oak, laurel, and, chestnut trees** are also found up to 7,000 feet above sea level.
 
• Pine trees are found up to 12,000 feet above sea level; above that point only lichens, grass, and moss can be found since it is so cold in the higher regions.

questions.question: What type of farming is Kumari which is practiced in Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primitive Subsistence farming.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primitive subsistence agriculture** is practiced on small patches of land with the help of primitive tools like hoe, dao, digging sticks, and family/ community labor.
 
• This type of farming depends upon monsoon, natural fertility of the soil, and suitability of other environmental conditions to the crops grown.
 
• Primitive subsistence farming makes use of primitive tools like digging sticks, dao, and hoe.
 
• The main crops are starchy foods such as tapioca, cassava or cassava, yams, corn or maize, millet, mountain rice, beans, and bananas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Plantations are a type of commercial farming where a single crop of tea, coffee, sugarcane, cashew, rubber, banana, or cotton is grown.
 
• Horticulture is the art of cultivating plants in gardens to produce food and medicinal ingredients, or for comfort and ornamental purposes.
 
• Horticulturists are agriculturists who grow flowers, fruits, and nuts, vegetables and herbs, as well as ornamental trees and lawns.
 
• Intensive farming focuses on investing a lot of resources and labor into small tracts of land in order to increase yield.

questions.question: Cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labor and capital is referred to as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**extensive cultivation.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Extensive cultivation refers to the practice of cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labor and capital. It is also known as extensive subsistence agriculture.**
 
• This type of cultivation is usually practiced in areas with low population density and abundant land resources.
 
• The main aim of extensive cultivation is to produce enough** food to meet the needs **of the family or community without the use of modern technology or intensive inputs.
 
• The crops grown in **extensive cultivation** are usually low-yielding and require less maintenance and care than in **intensive cultivation.**
 
• The other options are not correct because** hybrid cultivation** refers to the practice of growing genetically modified crops, intensive cultivation involves high inputs of labor and capital to produce high yields, and capitalist cultivation is a term used to** describe large-scale commercial farming done by corporations.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Hybrid cultivation** is a type of farming that involves the cross-breeding of two different plant varieties to create a new variety with desirable traits. This type of cultivation is often used to produce crops that are resistant to pests and diseases, have higher yields, and can tolerate harsh environmental conditions.
 
• ** Intensive cultivation** is a type of farming that involves high inputs of labor, capital, and technology to produce high yields of crops. This type of cultivation is often used in areas with high population density and limited land resources.
 
• **Capitalist cultivation** is a term used to describe the large-scale commercial farming done by corporations. This type of cultivation is often characterized by the use of modern technology, high inputs of labor and capital, and the production of crops for the global market.

questions.question: In 2018, India was the ______ producer of groundnut in the world.
questions.solution:

• **In 2018, India was the second largest **producer of groundnut in the world.
 
• The primary producers of **groundnuts (also known as peanuts) **are several countries around the world.
 
• The top producers of groundnuts globally include **China, India, Nigeria, the United States, Sudan, Senegal, Argentina, Myanmar, Indonesia, and Brazil.**
 
• **China and India **are the largest producers of groundnuts, accounting for a significant portion of the world's total production.
 
• These countries have favorable climates and large agricultural sectors that contribute to their high production levels.
 
• Nigeria is the leading producer of groundnuts in Africa, and it plays a vital role in the continent's overall production.
 
• The United States is also a major **producer, particularly in the southern states, such as Georgia, Texas, Alabama, and Florida.**

• The **Yellow Revolution** focuses on increasing the production of oilseeds to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oils.
 
• The **Round Revolution** is targeted at enhancing the production of potatoes, a staple food and an important cash crop.
 
• The **Golden Revolution** encompasses the overall development of horticulture, including fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and aromatic plants.
